messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Reserved pool 'dedicated-eu-west-1' queue growth > 500 in 5m, autoscaler throttle hit. Severity: P1. Affected tenants: 3 enterprise reservations. Metrics: reserved_gpu_util=100%, queue_len=542, autoscale_errors=RatelimitExceeded.
ops-oncall: paging @Eva Ramos @Raj Patel @Maya Chen. I'm on it, grabbing metrics now.
Eva Ramos: pulling logs, seeing repeated session init spikes from tenant 'VelvetPay' since 02:13 UTC. Thousands of short-lived sessions. Could be a runaway batch job.
Raj Patel: noted. Any evictions happening? autoscaler logs show "scale_up_rate_limited" and "quota_exceeded".
eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler: backoff=120s, current_replica_count=24, desired=40, max=24 (pool cap). No further replicas allowed under current reserved config.
Maya Chen: that max=24 limit is the reserved cap for that pool — enterprise reservation fully utilized. We need to either move overflow to shared pool or evict noisy tenant sessions.
Liam O'Connor: @Maya can you confirm which tenants are in the pool? I can run quick policy to deny new sessions for noisy tenant for 10m.
Maya Chen: tenants in pool: VelvetPay (enterprise), KoiHealth (enterprise), internal-testing (low priority). VelvetPay is spiking.
ops-oncall: rolling mitigation options: 1) apply tenant-level session throttle for VelvetPay, 2) temporarily route new VelvetPay sessions to hosted low-priority pool (if contractual ok), 3) manual eviction of idle sessions for internal-testing.
Eva Ramos: finding active sessions by tenant id -> snippet:
```
SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) as sessions, avg(latency) FROM session_registry
WHERE pool='dedicated-eu-west-1' AND started_at > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sessions DESC;
-- VelvetPay: 412, KoiHealth: 78, internal-testing: 53
```
Raj Patel: VelvetPay 412 sessions mostly short (<30s) so likely automated worker churn. Recommend immediate session deny for new VelvetPay jobs.
Liam O'Connor: executing deny rule: `reddctl routing rule add deny --tenant velvetpay --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --duration 600s --reason 'noisy-tenant emergency'`
eng-runtime-bot: command accepted, policy applied: deny new sessions for tenant velvetpay in pool dedicated-eu-west-1 (600s)
ops-oncall: also evicting internal-testing idle sessions to free slots.
Maya Chen: running eviction: `reddctl sessions evict --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --tenant internal-testing --idle-gt 30s --limit 60`
eng-runtime-bot: eviction started: 58 sessions evicted, reclaiming 6 GPUs-worth of concurrency.
ops-oncall: queue_len now 298. gpu_util still 100% but pressure reduced.
Eva Ramos: starting graceful fallback for KoiHealth if queue remains high: prepare to switch KoiHealth to model-compact-quant (smaller memory footprint) with no perf regressions expected for embeddings jobs.
account-success: @ops-oncall @Maya FYI I'm looped in. KoiHealth SLA allows failover within 15m, they must be notified. Drafting message.
customer-ops-bot: automatic customer bridge opened for affected tenants: VelvetPay (contact: onpager), KoiHealth (ops@koihealth.io). Bridge URL: https://bridge.internal/3801003456
Raj Patel: autoscaler still blocked by pool.max_replicas. Long term fix: raise reserved pool cap for this customer or enforce per-tenant concurrency guards. Short term: we can shift some reserved capacity to a burst pool if infra approves.
Liam O'Connor: I've requested temporary burst assignment to dedicated-eu-west-1-burst via infra runbook. infra-approver @SRE-Leads please ack.
SRE-Leads (system): ack requested. Approving temporary 6 GPU burst from standby cluster. ETA ~4m.
ops-oncall: applying burst: `infractl assign-burst --from standby-eu --to dedicated-eu-west-1 --gpus 6`
eng-runtime-bot: burst applied: +6 GPUs to pool. new max_replicas=30
ops-oncall: queue_len 120 -> 44 over next 3 minutes. autoscaler desired=32 allowed=30.
Eva Ramos: monitoring for reappearance. VelvetPay deny rule still preventing new sessions.
Maya Chen: KoiHealth completed fallback onto compact model, tail latency stable.
account-success: message sent to KoiHealth: short degraded performance mitigation active; we're shifting to compact model and will follow up with postmortem. They acknowledged.
VelvetPay-contact: onbridge: we observed a burst of job starts from an internal batch. Are you running a scheduled job? (VelvetPay replied: investigating, disabling batch)
ops-oncall: VelvetPay disabling batch reduced session starts to ~2/min. queue trending down.
eng-runtime-bot: reserve_pool_util=96%, queue_len=12, autoscale_errors resolved.
ops-oncall: all mitigations in place, removing deny rule in 8m if stable.
Maya Chen: prepare postmortem checklist: tenant-rate-limits, pool-sizing, autoscaler guards, operator runbook adjustments. Assigning follow-ups: Raj -> autoscaler rate limit telemetry; Eva -> per-tenant concurrency dashboard; Liam -> runbook to automate burst assignment.
account-success: I'll do customer follow-ups and provide timeline.
ops-oncall: incident resolved: pressure relieved, no SLA breaches recorded. Closing page in 10m unless regressions.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident cleared for reserved pool 'dedicated-eu-west-1'. Duration 00:47:04. Postmortem owner: Maya Chen. Reminder: create postmortem within 72h. :memo:
